input_payload: A customer's UPI AutoPay mandate for my subscription service failed with 'MANDATE_EXPIRED'. What happened and what should I do?
evidence_pool: UPI AutoPay mandates have a validity period set at creation; expired mandates cannot be debited.
NPCI mandate status API confirms mandate_id MPX8834 expired on 10 August 2026.
Customer was not sent a pre-expiry renewal reminder (merchant's notification setting was off).
Resolution: merchant must request customer to re-register mandate via the payment link.
NPCI allows mandate renewal within 30 days of creation date if merchant initiates.
ground_truth: Mandate MPX8834 expired on 10 August; customer must register a new mandate. Enable renewal reminders to prevent recurrence.

input_payload: I was charged a payment gateway fee of 2.5% on a government services transaction. Our agreement shows 0.5% for government category. Please clarify.
evidence_pool: Merchant's onboarding category: 'Government Services (Municipal Payments)' — MDR: 0.5%.
Transaction TXN99812 classified as category code 9399 (Government Services, General) — MDR 0.5% applies.
Invoice line shows 2.5% charged — investigation required.
Fee override applied by system: transaction tagged as 'Cross-border initiated' — MDR 2.5% triggered.
Customer's UPI app registered in Nepal; NPCI marks as cross-border, overriding merchant MDR.
ground_truth: Fee discrepancy caused by cross-border UPI transaction classification (customer UPI registered in Nepal); raise dispute for fee correction citing merchant MDR agreement.

input_payload: We offer monthly SaaS subscriptions (INR 999/month). What's the best payment method to reduce failed auto-debit attempts?
evidence_pool: UPI AutoPay success rate for recurring payments: 94.2% (RBI data, Q1 2026).
NACH e-mandate success rate: 89.7%; higher failure on first debit if bank verification pending.
Card recurring (SI) success rate: 87.1% for Indian-issued cards; depends on card limits.
UPI AutoPay allows pre-debit notifications 24h before, reducing customer surprises.
Amount INR 999 is below UPI AutoPay limit of INR 1 lakh for recurring mandates.
ground_truth: Recommend UPI AutoPay: highest success rate (94.2%), mandatory pre-debit notifications reduce disputes, and INR 999 is well within limits.

input_payload: My merchant account was put on 'rolling reserve' hold — 10% of settlements withheld for 180 days. Is this standard? Can it be reduced?
evidence_pool: Rolling reserve is standard practice for high-risk merchant categories or new merchants with limited history.
Merchant category: 'Travel — OTA' (MCC 4722) — classified high-risk for chargebacks.
Merchant's chargeback rate last 90 days: 1.8% (industry threshold: 1.0%).
Rolling reserve can be reviewed after 6 months of compliant operation.
Reduction criteria: chargeback rate below 0.5% for 3 consecutive months.
ground_truth: Rolling reserve is standard for OTA merchants with 1.8% chargeback rate (above 1% threshold). Reduction possible after 6 months if chargeback rate falls below 0.5% for 3 consecutive months.
